name: count the steps before you build the ladder
one_line: Two words of the same length, and how many steps it will take is worked out by counting before anybody tries to get from one to the other.
how: Print two words of one length, one above the other — CANE and CASA — with a row of boxes underneath. Before any solving, ask in how many positions they differ. That number is the least number of steps there can be, because one step fixes at most one position, and it is got by counting and needs no dictionary. Then print the ladder as blanks, one word to a rung, every rung a real word. Then let the person choose their own pair and do the same. Print the warning: the ladder may not exist. Of 5 757 English words of five letters, 671 have no neighbour one letter away; in Italian nobody has counted.

knobs.knob: whether the least number is asked for first
knobs.effect: Asked first, the sheet yields one exact number before anything is solved, and it survives even when the ladder never comes. Asked afterwards it is arithmetic about a finished answer and teaches nothing.

knobs.knob: how far apart the two words are
knobs.effect: Differing in two positions is a two-rung ladder and a start. Four is long enough that most attempts die halfway, and there is no way to know in advance whether any path exists at all.
A pair chosen by the sheet has been walked and works. A pair chosen by the person may have no ladder, and saying so in advance turns the dead end into a result rather than a failure.
Same length keeps the count of differing positions defined and the exercise with it. Allowing letters in and out makes the ladder easier and makes the printed number mean nothing.

where_the_work_is: In the pair, which has to be walked before it is printed. The count of differing positions is free and exact; whether a path exists is neither, and that is the half that fails.
breaks: Ink, and it prints. On 800x480 the two words and the count each fit on one line, which is rare here. Scanned back the rungs read if the boxes are ruled. Composing is where it goes wrong: a model offers a pair with no path and cannot tell, so walk the ladder by hand and keep the pair you walked.
